*Mātṛsvasā*. Here, by the rule *ātṛpitṛbhyāṃ svaseḥ*, the substitution of *ṣ* does not occur. If it is objected: "In that case, the previously mentioned forms *bāhuṣu* and *śvāśurī* would not be established," do not say so.
For, since no specific words are mentioned in the rule for the suffixes *aṇ* and *iñ*, that [substitution] applies even to those [words] which are not well-known [in this context].
And it should be stated that [the suffix] applies to *vyāsa*, *varuḍa*, *niṣāda*, *caṇḍāla*, and *bimba*. Regarding *vyāsa*:

he who arranges (*vyasyati*) the Vedas is *vedavyāsa*. [The suffix] *aṇ* is applied according to the rule *karmanyaṇ*. This is a case of designating a part by the whole, as in the expression *bhīma* for *bhīmasena*.

(904) *na yvābhyām padāntābhyāṃ pūrvau tu tābhyām aic* | P. 7.3.3. [The vowels] *ai* and *au* are not substituted [for *e* and *o*] when they follow *y* or *v* that stand at the end of a word; however, those two (*ai* and *au*) are substituted for *e* and *o* when they are preceded by *y* or *v*. Why "by *y* or *v*"? Consider: *nārthiḥ*. [Derivation: *na arthaḥ yasya* = *nārthaḥ*; his descendant is *nārthiḥ*. Why "at the end of a word"? Consider: *yājñikaḥ*. The mention of *aic* is for the purpose of indicating the scope [of the rule].

The word ‘e’ expresses a prohibition. Therefore, in this case, there is no [vṛddhi]: *dāghyaśviḥ*, *mādhvaśviḥ*. For here, there is no possibility of vṛddhi following [the vowels] *y* and *v*. However, even when the possibility of vṛddhi exists, it is not desired in certain instances: *dvyāśītikaḥ*, meaning one who was hired for, has been hired for, or will be hired for eighty-two [pieces].

Regarding *vāruḍaki*: *vāruḍa* and the others are specific sub-castes (*jāti-viśeṣa*). Because the letter *v* is not at the end of a word, the substitution *aij* (i.e., *ai*) applies by the rule *ayvābhyām*. "And so forth" refers to: *naiṣādakiḥ*, *cāṇḍālakiḥ*, *baimbakiḥ*.
(905) Pāṇini 4.1.98: *gotre kuñjādibhyaś cphañ*. [The suffix *cphañ* is applied after the words *kuñja* and others when forming patronymics denoting a lineage.]

*Kuñja* is used for *gotra*. They say that if the two preceding sūtras beginning with "ṭhakau gotre" were recited, then the mention of *gotra* here could have been omitted. The letter *ñ* in *cphañ* is for the purpose of causing *vṛddhi*. [The example is] *Kauñjāyanyaḥ*. The letter *c*, however, is for the sake of [the rule] "ṭh-vrāta-cphañ-au."
This is for the purpose of specification. By means of this, in the case of *aśvādibhyaḥ phañ* (Pāṇini 4.1.110), as in *āśvayanaḥ*, the suffix *ñya* does not occur.

Here, the following should be noted: in forms such as *kauñjāyanyaḥ*, whether in the singular or the dual, because the suffix *ñya* contains the indicatory letter *ñ*, there is only the acute accent on the first syllable (*ādyaudātatvam*). However, in the plural, when there is the elision (*luk*) of *ñya*—

When there is a conflict between two rules of equal strength regarding the letters *c* and *ph*, as well as the letter *ā*, the rule for the acute accent (*udātta*) on the first syllable by means of the *ñit-svara* would apply due to its posteriority; however, in the *Bhāṣya* and other works, having split the rule at "kitah" in the phrase "addhitasya kitah" and carried forward the term "itaḥ," [the rule is applied] to that which is not a secondary derivative (*addhita*).

Because of the explanation that "the word *cita* [indicates] an acute accent on the final syllable," in the case of *auñjhāyanāḥ*, there is indeed an acute accent on the final syllable. Nor should it be argued: "In this case, let there simply be the suffix *phak*; what is the use of this cumbersome designation? For if that were so, [the following would occur].

Because of the formulation of the rule *vrātaprakorastriyām* (Pāṇini 4.1.142), the suffix *ñya* would also apply after [names] such as Nāḍāyana and others. For example: *kuñja*, *vradhna*, *śaṅkha*, *śakaṭa*, etc.
(906) *vrātañphañorastriyām* |5|3|113|.

Regarding *vrātacphañ*: because the phrase “*ñyaḥ* after words meaning ‘a troop (*vrāta*)’ and ‘a leader (*agramaṇī*)’” follows from the previous rule, he says “*ñyaḥ* should be [the suffix]. He will give *kāpotapākyaḥ* as an example for words expressing a *vrāta*. Why does it say “not in the feminine (*astriyām*)”? [Consider] *kapotapākā* as a woman. This is because they are *tadrāja* suffixes; for it is said that “*ñya*-type suffixes and others are *tadrāja* suffixes.”

The word "by the sūtra" is the ellipsis [to be supplied]. "It will be stated that there is elision" means by the rule "adrājasya bahuṣu" (Pāṇini 2.4.62); this is the ellipsis. Regarding *kauñjāyanī*: they say that here, when the suffix *ñya* is present, because it has *y* as its penultimate letter (*yopadha*), the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is excluded by the rule "ātaḥ" (Pāṇini 4.1.40), and thus a difference should be understood both in the form and in the accent.

(907) *yañiñośca* |4|1|101|. The term *gotra*, which is obtained through the governing context (*adhikāra*), qualifies *yañ* and *iñ*, but not the suffix *phak* which is being prescribed; this is because of the [traditional] commentary. This is what [the author] expresses by saying "as far as *gotra*. Regarding *gotra*:
What [is the purpose]? [It is to ensure that] the suffix *yañ* applies in the sense of "born on an island" (*dvīpe bhavaḥ*) to form *dvaupyaḥ*.

Furthermore, the suffix *iñ*, which is prescribed in four senses after words such as *sutaṅgama*, would apply to form *sautaṅgamiḥ*. [The rule would otherwise prevent] the application of the suffix *phak* to his descendant.
[The phrase] "lest there be *phak*" implies that this [suffix *yañ*] is applied by virtue of its capacity (*sāmarthyāt*).
(908) *śaradvac-chunaka-darbha-bhṛgu-vatsa-āgrāyaṇeṣu* |4|1|102| In the case of *śaradvat*, *śunaka*, *darbha*, *bhṛgu*, *vatsa*, and *āgrāyaṇa*, [the suffix *iñ* is applied].

The offspring of *śaradvat* is not [denoted by] *śaradvataḥ*, because [the latter] was already formed previously. Likewise, *vatsaḥ* is not the offspring of *śunaka*. Therefore, in this context, it is *bhārgavaḥ*.

In the dvandva compound *vātsyaśca āgrāyaṇaśca*, the elision (*luk*) should be understood as applicable according to the rules "atribhṛgu" and "ṭhyañiñośca," as appropriate. Although in this case the elision by the rule "atribhṛgu" etc. is difficult to obtain due to the absence of plurality (*bahutva*), nevertheless, [it applies] when there is simultaneous expression of the substratum (*yugapadadhikaraṇavacanatā*).

Because the constituent words have multiple meanings, or because it is a *sūtra*-style expression, there may indeed be elision (*luk*). Therefore, he explains: "if [the patronymic] Bhārgava," and "if [the patronymic] Vātsya.
(Pāṇini 4.1.103) *droṇaparvatajīvantād anyatarasyām*.

Regarding the term *anādi*: the meaning is that this Droṇa is indeed different from the one well-known in the Mahābhārata as the father of Aśvatthāman. Regarding the phrase *aśvatthāmni* and so forth: the usage *rauṇāyana* applied to Aśvatthāman—the immediate descendant of the teacher Droṇa—is figurative.

(910) *anṛṣyānantarye bidādibhyo ’ñ* |4|1|104|. "Anṛṣya-" [is used]; there is a Vedic elision (*luk*) of the fifth case-ending in the word "anṛṣi," meaning "from those who are not seers" (*anṛṣibhyaḥ*). In the sūtra, "ānantarye" means "in the sense of immediate succession. "Svārthe" means "in its own sense."

The intention is that [the list] beginning with *cāturvarṇya* belongs to the class of *ākṛtigaṇas*. Regarding the form *baida*, he anticipates the objection that the suffix *aṇ* [prescribed after] seers (*ṛṣi*) might apply, and thus says: "from the *bāhu*-class, etc. [The members of this class are: *vida*, *urva*, *kaśyapa*, *kuśika*, *bharadvāja*, *upamanyu*, *viśvānara*, and so forth, according to the rule: "and *arastrī* and *paraśu*," etc.

(911) Pāṇini 4.1.105: *gargādibhyo yañ* || [The suffix] *yañ* is applied after [the group of names] beginning with Garga. [The list begins: Garga, Vatsa, Vyāghrapāda, Pulista, Babhru, Maṇḍu, Vataṇḍa, Kapi, Kata, Śakala, Kaṇva, Agasti, Kuṇḍina, Yajñavalka, Parāśara.

"Jamadagni," and so forth. How then is it that [the term] "Rāma Jāmadagnya" is used? For this [suffix -yañ] applies to the immediate descendant. True; however, it should be understood that even for an immediate descendant, the designation of a *gotra* (clan name) is superimposed upon him.
(Pāṇini 2.4.64): *yañañoś ca*.

Regarding *yañañośca*: from the rule *ṭhṇyakṣatriyārṣe’tya* [Pāṇini 2.4.62], the word *luk* is understood; from the rule *tadrājasya* [Pāṇini 2.4.62], the phrases *bahuṣu* and *tenaivā’striyām* are carried over by anuvṛtti; and from the rule *yaskādibhyo gotre* [Pāṇini 2.4.63], the word *gotre* is also carried over.
(913) *madhubabhvrór brāhmaṇakauśikayoḥ* |4|1|106|.

Regarding the rule "if it ends in *yañ* in the sense of a *gotra*" and so forth: since the suffixes *yañ* and *añ* alone do not denote a *gotra* as established in the *Pravarādhyāya*, but rather only when they are combined with other elements, the term "*gotra*" here qualifies that which ends in those suffixes (*tadanta*).
Regarding the phrase *tadavayavayoḥ*: the intention is that "substitutes occur for that which is being specifically indicated.

Regarding the phrase *pravarādhyāya*: the intention is that this was stated by Kaiyaṭa, having cited the Bhāṣya on the rule *trīpuṃsābhyām*, which says, "there is the inclusion of the non-technical (laukika) gotra."

Regarding "lohitādīti": by the rule beginning with "arvatra lohitādī," the suffix *ṣpha* is applied. Although the feminine gender is already expressed by *ṣpha*, he says "bābhravyāyaṇī" with the intention that the suffix *ṅīṣ* is added due to the force of the *ṣ*-marker.
Indeed, the reading "babhruḥ, kauśika" occurs within the *gargādi* group itself; for it is in this way that there is a double mention of *babhru*.
"It should not be formed," so say Haradatta and others.
(914) Regarding *kāpeya* in [Pāṇini 4.1.107] *kapibodhād āṅgirase*: the suffix *ḍhak* is applied by [the rule] *itaś cāniñaḥ*. The word *kapi* is listed in the *gargādi* group.
The purpose [of the suffix] is for the sake of denoting effects such as "red" (*lohita*). By means of this, *Kātyāyanī* is established; likewise, *Baudhī*.
Because [the base] is not a seer (*anṛṣi*), the suffix *iñ* is applied, or alternatively, because it belongs to the *bāhv-ādi* group.
(915) [Pāṇini 4.1.108: *vataṇḍācca*.

[The rule] "and from Vataṇḍa" is a restrictive rule (*niyamārtha*) intended to ensure that when the suffixes *yañ* and *aṇ* are applicable [to the patronymic of Vataṇḍa], only *yañ* is used for one belonging to the Aṅgiras lineage.
(916) *luk striyām* 1.4.109. [This rule prescribes the elision of the patronymic suffix in the feminine.]

"Elision (luk) occurs in the feminine. Regarding "of that which has been prescribed": it should be understood as "or of that which remains after [the application of] aṇ. And this is obtained through the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule "in the case of Āṅgirasa. Although one might form a single sūtra as "elision in the feminine after vataṇḍa," because the phrase "in the case of Āṅgirasa" would not be discontinued, [the elision would apply] even when it is not an Āṅgirasa.

Although the desired form is established for the feminine because of the absence of the elision (*luk*) of *yañ* and *aṇ*, nevertheless, since both *yañ* and *aṇ* would undesirably apply to the masculine *Āṅgirasa*, a separate rule was composed to prevent that.

[The phrase] "because of being a seer" (*ṛṣitvāt*) means: and it is not as if [the form] were already established by the *aṇ* suffix in the rule "after *ṛṣi*, *andhaka*, etc. (*ṛṣy-andhake’ṇ*), [since] in the *śivādi* group...

It should not be suspected that the recitation of *vataṇḍī* is useless; for since the suffix *yañ* would otherwise supersede it due to its inclusion in the *gargādi* group, the recitation of that [term] is necessary to prevent such a supersession. The phrase "not after *ṣyaṅ*" refers to the rule *ṭhaṇiñoranārṣayor guraavamanuṣyanāmnoḥ prācām*.

(917) *Aśvādibhyaḥ phañ* | Pāṇini 4.1.110. From the group beginning with *aśva*: [the suffix *phañ* is applied] when a *gotra* [is to be expressed]. In this list (*gaṇa*), three words ending in *gotra*-suffixes are recited: *bailva*, *anāḍuhya*, and *ātreyi*; however, from these, [the suffix is applied] only for the *yuvan* [generation]. As it is said: "There is only one [suffix] in the *gotra*."

From the statement “*otrād yaūnī*,” [the suffix] *yaūni* is applied there; from *bili-* [derived from] *vṛddha-aitosala-* [with the suffix] *ñyaṅ*; the word *ānaḍuhya-* ends in *ñ*; it should be understood that the word *ātreya-* ends in *ḍak*. “Born as a male” (*puṃsi jātaḥ*)—this is a *gaṇasūtra*.
The meaning is that [the suffix] *phañ* occurs when the word *jāta* exists as a masculine.
When there is an expectancy (*ākāṅkṣā*) as to "from what?", it is understood from the sense (*arthāt*) to be "from the word *jāta*. Regarding the form *jātāyāḥ*:

this is either by the *liṅgaviśiṣṭaparibhāṣā* (the rule concerning forms qualified by gender) or because the single substitute (*ekādeśa*) is included as part of the preceding element (*pūrvāntatvena*).
[The suffix] *prāptiḥ*.
(918) Pāṇini 4.1.112: *śivādibhyo’ṇ* [the suffix *aṇ* is applied after words beginning with *śiva*]. But surely—

Since the suffix *aṇ* will certainly apply by virtue of the very fact that [the rule] is formulated, setting aside the specific suffixes such as *iñ* and others, what is the purpose of this explicit mention of *aṇ*? Regarding this, they say: the word *ṛṣiṣeṇa* is recited in this list;
therefore, having set aside the *miñ* which would otherwise apply, the suffix *ṇya*—characterized by the ending *-enā-*—would apply by virtue of its higher priority.
In this case, by the force of the recitation [of the rule], only the suffix *iñ* as it is obtained [by the previous rule] would apply, and not *aṇ*.

Thus, some hold that the mention of *aṇ* here is necessary. Others hold that because *aṇ* is the governing topic (*adhikāra*), only *aṇ* would apply and no other; therefore, the mention of *aṇ* is for the sake of clear understanding. [The examples are: Śibi, Kakutstha, Vataṇḍa.

Jaratkāru, Vipāṭ, Takṣan, Viśravas, Ravaṇa, Ṛṣiṣeṇa, Virūpākṣa, and so forth. The word *gotra* (lineage) is understood [to apply here]. This is established in the *Vṛtti* and in Kaiyaṭa’s commentary. Although it is said that "the section concerning *gotra* extends up to the rule defining the technical term *gotra*," [this applies] regarding the *yuvan* suffixes.
This is understood from both the Bhāṣya and Kaiyaṭa on the *Lugviti* sūtra; nevertheless, the sense is that this is a different opinion.
Thus it is established that from this point onward, suffixes occur in the general sense of offspring.
Since the suffix *ḍhak* would necessarily apply after *śubhra* due to its being a word ending in *at*, the word *jaratkāru* is recited here for the sake of the suffix *aṇ*.

From *Jāratkārava*: by the rule "ḍhaki tu ‘heya-lopo’kardvāḥ” (Pāṇini 6.4.153), there is elision of the *ū* [of *ūru*], resulting in *Jāratkāreya*. Since the class beginning with *kuñja* applies the suffix *cphañ* invariably by the rule “otre kuñjādibhyaḥ,” the word *vipāṭ* is recited here for the sake of the suffix *aṇ*; thus, *vaipāśa*.

*Vaipāśāyanyaḥ*. Regarding the rule *enāntalakṣaṇe* (Pāṇini 4.1.152), which prescribes the suffix *ṇya*, the suffix *iñ* would otherwise apply by the rule *udīcām* (Pāṇini 4.1.153). However, the word *takṣan* is listed here for the purpose of [introducing] the suffix *aṇ*; it is intended that both suffixes coexist here through the application of *ṇya*, but not through *iñ*. Thus: *tākṣṇaḥ* and *tākṣaṇyaḥ*.
The forms *viśravaṇa* and *rāvaṇa* are taught here; these two are substitutes for the word *viśravas*.
The offspring (*apatyam*) of *viśravas* is *vaiśravaṇaḥ* and *rāvaṇaḥ*.
(919) Pāṇini 4.1.113: *nadīmānuṣībyastannāmikābhyaḥ*. [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after feminine names of rivers and human females.]

With the intention that it would have been more appropriate to formulate the rule as "from non-vṛddha [names] of rivers and female humans who are non-vṛddha," he explains by means of the words beginning with "from non-vṛddha" (*avṛddhebhyaḥ*). Regarding "Ātreya":
the sense is that this [suffix], being subsequent, supersedes the *ṛṣyaṇ* suffix.

(920) *māturutsaṅkhyāsaṃbhadrapūrvāyāḥ* |4|1|115|. [The suffix *ṣyaṅ* is applied after the word *mātṛ* when it is preceded by the word *dvi*, a numeral, or the words *saṃ* and *bhadra*. For example, *dvaimāturaḥ*. This is a compound formed by the rule *addhitārtha* etc. (*Pāṇini* 2.1.51). Here, the analysis (*vigraha*) is "the offspring of two mothers" (*dvayormātrorapatyam*), and not "the offspring of two [different] mothers" (*dvimātrorapatyam*).
Because of the rule "in the case of a numeral [compounded] with a word denoting a name," a compound is impossible when it is not a name;

hence the example *dhānyamātuḥ*. Although it would have been established by the rule *abhivyaktapadārthāḥ* that only a word denoting a mother is intended, the intention is that the feminine gender designation is for the sake of clear understanding.
Others, however, say that [the word *kanyā*] is for the purpose of making known the non-eternality (*anityatā*) of the term "manifested" (*abhivyakta*).
Pāṇini 4.1.116: *kanyāyāḥ kanīna ca*.
[The commentary asks: Regarding the word *kanyā*: surely a *kanyā* is one whose virginity (*akṣatayoni*) is intact; and for her, the production of offspring (*apatya-sambhava*) is simply impossible.
Fearing that [the rule] might not apply, he says: "of one who is unmarried" (*anūḍhāyāḥ*). This means: of one who has not been married.

(923) *Vikarṇa-śuṅga-cchagalāt* [the suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after *vatsa*, *bharadvāja*, and *atri*. 4.1.117. [The rule applies] to *vikarṇa*; when there is a *dvandva* compound of words ending in patronymic suffixes such as *vatsya* and others, [the suffix *ṭhak* is applied] by [the rule] *ṭhyañañośca*.

In the two sūtras beginning with *ṭha-tribhṛgu-kutsa*, there is elision (*luk*) of the patronymic suffix (*apatya-pratyaya*). One should not suspect that here there could be a copulative compound (*dvandva*) of Vatsa and the others alone; for those who constitute the root [of the lineage] do not stand in the relation of offspring (*apatya*) toward those such as Vikarman. Therefore, he explains: "Vātsya," and so forth.
That "there is plurality when there is simultaneous expression of multiple substrates" has been stated in the very sūtra *aradvaśunakam* (Pāṇini 2.4.12).
[The suffix *cha* is applied] optionally after the word *pīlā*. (Pāṇini 4.1.118)
In this context, the suffix is *iñ*. The intention is that the word "or" (*vā*) is carried over from the preceding rule.
(925) *strībhyo ḍhak* | P. 4.1.120.
Regarding *strībhyo ḍhak*: because of the use of the plural number in the citation, there is no reference to the verbal form itself, nor to its meaning.

Because the word *vimātṛ* is listed among the *śubhrādi* group for the sake of its specific meaning (*ḍhag-arthatayā*), however, the intention is that there is a reference to the *ṭāp* and other suffixes taught under the heading of feminine (*stryadhikāra*), and not to the *ktin* and others which are separated from that context; with this in mind, he says "from those ending in feminine suffixes," and so forth. By that—

In the case of the example "arada-patyaṃ dāradaḥ," the suffix *ḍhak* does not apply. However, if the term "stryartha" (feminine sense) were included [in the rule], then *ḍhak* would indeed apply here. For the word *darad* denotes both a country (*janapada*) and a Kṣatriya; from it, in the sense of offspring, the suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule "yañ-magadha... (Pāṇini 4.1.170). When that [suffix] is elided in the feminine by the rule "ataśca" (Pāṇini 4.1.173), the form *darad* remains.

Because it denotes a feminine object. While the rule *hak ca* is still in effect, the repetition of *ḍhak* here is for the purpose of excluding the *ḍhak* that is not connected with *aṇ*. Although, by the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*) "that which is drawn forward does not apply further on," *aṇ* does not operate here, nevertheless—of that [rule]...
They say that the inclusion of the suffix *ḍhak* is for the purpose of making known its impermanence (*anityatva*).
(Pāṇini 4.3.121) *vyañcaḥ*.

[The suffix *aṇ* is applied] in the sense of "belonging to this" (*tasyedam*). Others hold that because it belongs to the *śiva*-class, the suffix *aṇ* applies only in the sense of "offspring" (*apatya*).

(927) *itaś cāniñaḥ* |4|1|122|. [The suffix] *añ* is applied after a word ending in *it*, provided that it does not already end in the suffix *ini*. Why "ending in *it*"? Consider *dākṣiḥ* (the son of Dakṣa). Why "provided it does not end in *ini*"? Consider *dākṣāyaṇaḥ* (the descendant of Dakṣa). Why "after a word consisting of two syllables"? Consider *audadhiḥ* (the offspring of Udadhi). However, in the *Kāśikā*:

The statement that "the form *arīceḥ* [is derived] from *mārīcaḥ*" is incorrect. This is because the suffix *iñ* applies by virtue of [the word] belonging to the *bāhv-ādi* group. Nor is its inclusion in the *bāhv-ādi* group unestablished, for it is stated in the Bhāṣya on the sūtra "idaco ’ntyātparaḥ" (Pāṇini 1.1.47) that "the word *arīci* is recited among the *bāhv-ādi* group."

(928) *Śubhrādibhyaś ca* |4|1|123|. They say that the word *ca* ("and") is intended to indicate that this is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class of words). The word *mṛkaṇḍa* is recited here [in the list]. Examples: *Mārkaṇḍeya*. The list begins with: *śubhra*, *mṛkaṇḍa*, *aśva*, *vimātṛ*.

"Vidhavā," "godhā," "pravāhaṇā," and so forth. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class). By this, forms such as "āṇḍaveya" are established. Here, among the words ending in short vowels (*adanta*), the suffix *iñ* would otherwise have been applicable; however, from the word *vidhavā*, the suffix *ḍhak* applies by virtue of its being a term denoting a low-caste woman (*kṣudrā*), and for words denoting four-footed species, the suffix *ḍhañ* applies.
From the word *godhā*, the suffix *ḍhrañ* is also applied after *vana*; it should be understood that in some cases the general suffix *aṇ* would otherwise have been applicable.
(929) *pravāhaṇasya ḍhea* | 7|3|28|.

The suffix *ḍhea* is applied after *pravāhaṇa*. The rule *uttarapadasya* is governed [by this]. From the rule *ṭhardhātparimāṇāt*, the phrase *pūrvastha tu vā* is carried over [into this context]. Thus he says: "of the vowels at the beginning of the *uttarapada*," and so forth. However, the result of the compulsory (*nitya*) *vṛddhi* of the *uttarapada* is as follows:
In the example *‘ravāhaṇeyībhāryaḥ’*, there is a prohibition of the masculine-like treatment (*puṃvadbhāva*) by the rule *‘vṛddhinimittasya’*.
(930) *tatpratyayasya ca* | 7|2|29|. The phrase *‘ravāhaṇasya’* is understood [from the previous rule]. By the word *tad* (that), the suffix *ḍha* is referred to.
It is referred to [by the word *parāmṛśyate*]. Thus he says: "of that which ends in *ḍhak*, etc. Regarding the phrase "caused by an external *iñ*":
the meaning is "caused by that *iñ* suffix which occurs outside [the formation] ending in the suffix *ḍhak*. (Pāṇini 4.1.126) *kalyāṇyādīnāminaṅ*.

[The suffix] *kalyāṇy-ādīnām* [is applied]. Here, the word *parastrī* is recited. It is a genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*) meaning "the wife of another" (*parasya strī parastrī*). [From this,] *pārastraiṇeyaḥ* [is derived], meaning "born from the wife of another. There is vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) in both members of the compound because it belongs to the *anuśatikādi* group. However, in the *bidādi* list, [it is read as] *arastrī paraśuṃ*...

Thus it is read; "he obtains" (*rāpnoti*) is the ellipsis to be supplied. In that context, *parā* (other) and *strī* (woman) form a *karmadhāraya* compound. The offspring of another’s wife is a *pāraśava*; he is born from a Brāhmaṇa father and a Śūdra mother who was married by him. And she is called "another’s wife" because of her connection with a different caste (*jātyantara*). Nor... [is it] so.

It should not be argued that because of the *sthānivadbhāva* (the status of being like the original) of the substitute *paraśva*, there would be *ubhayapada-vṛddhi* (vṛddhi of both members) even in the case of *pāraśava* by the rule *anuśatikādīnāṃ ca*; for when there is a substitute, the original prior and posterior members are obscured, and thus that rule does not apply. In this list (*gaṇa*), the suffix *ḍhak* is applied to words ending in feminine suffixes.

The mention [of these terms] is for the sake of establishing their status as *siddha* (already established), whereas for others it serves both purposes. Examples include *kalyāṇī*, *subhagā*, *durbhagā*, *bandhakī*, *parastrī*, and so forth.
(932) Or, in the case of *kulaṭā*, [the suffix ṅīṣ is optionally applied]. 4.1.127.

Or [the form] *kaulaṭāyāḥ* is derived from *kulaṭā* by the rule of *pararūpa* (substitution of the subsequent vowel) as in the case of *śakandhu*, or by specific irregular derivation (*nipātana*). Thus, *satī* and *bhikṣukī* are used [as feminine bases]. In this context, regarding the prescription of the suffix *anaṅ*: so it has been stated by Amara— "Now, *bāndhakineyaḥ* and *bandhulaḥ* are the sons of an unchaste woman (*asatī*); [also] *kaulaṭeraḥ* and *kaulaṭīyaḥ*."

But if she is a virtuous woman (satī), then her son is called *kolaṭīnaya* or *kaulaṭeya*. Some, however, maintain that the suffix *inaṅ* also forms a third form, *kaulaṭineya*, even from the word *kṣudrā*. The sense is that the suffix *ḍhak* also occurs in this alternative case.

(933) *hadbhagasindhvante pūrvapadasya ca* | 7|3|19| In the rule *hadbhada*, the word *ca* ("and") from the phrase *pūrvapadasya ca* is drawn forward [to this sūtra] by means of the particle *ca*. Therefore, he says: "of both the preceding and the following members. This applies in cases such as *mahate saubhagāya*.

The suffix *añ* is applied because [the word] belongs to the *udrātra*-class; the intention is that there is no *vṛddhi* of the subsequent syllable due to its being Vedic (*chāndasa*). Anticipating the objection that—since the rule "aṭakāyāḥ ṛ" specifies the feminine gender—the suffix would not apply in the masculine, he says: "It should be stated as 'caṭakasya'. Thus, and so forth.
The statement by the author of the *Nyāsa* that "aṭakādairagi" is the traditional reading should be disregarded because it contradicts the *Vārttika*.

[In the case of] a feminine descendant, the elision (*luk*) must be stated. [This applies] to those two [suffixes] alone. In that regard, when there is elision of the secondary suffix (*taddhita-luk*) after a word ending in *ṭāp*:

The meaning is that, when there is elision (*luk*) of the feminine suffix *ṭāp* by the rule "after a word ending in an *uṇādi* suffix or a *taddhita* suffix," the suffix *ṅīṣ*, which is conditioned by [the word being] a genus (*jāti*), is set aside, and instead the suffix *ṭāp* is applied, conditioned by [the word ending in] a vowel beginning with *a*.
(934) Pāṇini 4.1.129: *godhāyā ḍhrak*.
Regarding *gaudhera*: when the substitution of *ey* for *ḍha* has been made, there is the elision of *y* by the rule *opo vyoḥ*. (Pāṇini 6.1.115).
[The sūtra] *āragudīcām* (Pāṇini 4.1.130):

"The suffix *āraṅ* [is applied] according to the Northerners. Since the alternative application of the suffixes *ḍhraṅ* and *ḍhaka* is already established by the very wording [of the rule], [the mention of the Northerners is for the sake of restriction].

The mention of "northerners" (udīcām) is for the sake of honor. The rule was not formulated as *arak*, because if the vowel *ā* were elided by the rule *yasyeti ca*, the undesirable form *audharaḥ* would result. "From another" means from some [base] other than one ending in *ā*, according to the requirements of the specific grammatical examples (*lakṣya*). Regarding *paṇḍasya*: *paṇḍaḥ*...
A eunuch; his offspring, however, is designated as *kṛtrima* ("artificial") and so forth.
(936) *Kṣudrābhyo vā* | Pāṇini 4.1.131. Regarding *kṣudrābhyaḥ*: the feminine gender residing in the meaning is superimposed upon the word, hence the mention of the feminine gender (*strīliṅga*).
(937) *gṛṣṭyādibhyaśca* |4|1|136|. From *gṛṣṭi* and others: *gṛṣṭi*, *hṛṣi*, *hali*, *bali*, *krudri*, *agasti*, *mitrayu*.
This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the suffix] *aṇ*. Here, because the last two [names] refer to sages (*ṛṣi*), the suffix *aṇ* would otherwise be applicable.

The distinction is that for others, the suffix is *ḍhak* according to the rule "ṭhitaśca-aniñaḥ. Thus, we have *gārṣṭeya*. A *gṛṣṭi* is any cow that has calved once, not necessarily a cow (*go*) alone; therefore, the suffix *ḍhañ* is not established here by the rule "aṇ-catur-pād-bhyaḥ."

(938) *kekaya-mitrayu-pralayānāṃ yāder iyaḥ* | 7|3|2| [The suffix *yañ* applied to] *kekaya*, *mitrayu*, and *pralaya* is changed to *iy* when it begins with *y*. *kekaya*: the feminine descendant of *kekaya* is *kekayī*. [This is derived by: “*añ* is added after a *kṣatriya* name that does not end in *pada*,” and then “*yañ* is added. She is censured by means of *aitreyikā*. The meaning is: "by the state of being a *mitrayu*."
The suffix *vuñ* is applied [by the rule] "after *gotra*, *caraṇa*, *chala*, and *ātyāya*, there is *vuñ*. For in that context, the worldly *gotra* is understood;

and in common usage, the word *ṛṣi* is well known as a *gotra*. This is so when the word *mitrayu*, by way of metaphorical identification (*abhedopacāra*), refers to the lineage of his descendants. Thus says the *Kāśikā*. And this... [is the case] when...
This is to be understood; otherwise, there would be no analysis here using the plural form *yūnām*.

[The word] *rāleyam* means "that which has come from *pralaya*. The substitution of *iy* does not sublate the *vṛddhi* [vowel], because their spheres of application are distinct: the rule "there is *vṛddhi* for the first vowel of a *ṭha*-affix" and the rule "the substitution of *iy* for that which begins with *ya*" apply to different domains.
Haradatta maintains that the *aṅga* (the stem) is the qualifier for both [the suffix and the substitute], but it is not the object of the operation (*kāryin*).
Others, however, argue: "Let this very sūtra be the prescriptive rule even for the initial *vṛddhi* (P. 7.2.1); what is the use of this investigation into the distinction of domains?"

(939) *dāṇḍināyanahāstināyanātharvaṇikajaihmāśineyavāśināyanibhrauṇahatyadhaibatyasāravaikṣvākamaitreyahiraṇmayāni* || 6.4.174 || The forms *dāṇḍināyana*, etc., are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*). From *daṇḍin* and *hastin*— from these two [the suffix *phak* is applied].

The suffix *phak* is applied because [the word] belongs to the *naḍādi* group; the absence of *ṭilopa* (elision of the final vowel) occurs by virtue of a specific grammatical rule (*nipātana*). In the list beginning with *vasantādi*, the form *atharvan* is recited. By metaphorical usage, the text proclaimed by Atharvan is called "Atharvan"; one who studies that is an *ātharvaṇika*. In the *śubhrādi* group, the form *ihmāśin* is recited.

His offspring is *jaihmāśineya*. The offspring of *vāśin* is *vāśināyaniḥ*. According to the rule "the suffix *phiñ* [is applied] after a *vṛddha* [stem], according to the usage of the Northern grammarians," [the forms are derived]. In the case of *bhrūṇahan* and *dhīvan*, when the suffix *ṣyañ* is applied, the substitution of *t* for the final letter is prescribed as an irregularity (*nipātana*). Thus, the state of being a killer of an embryo (*bhrūṇahan*) is *bhrauṇahatyam*.

Regarding *dhaivatyam*: although the substitution of *t* for *han* is already established by the rule *ṭhano’sta’ciṇṇaloḥ*, the explicit mention of the letter *t* (*takāra-nipātana*) indicates the following principle: "When a verbal root is mentioned by its own form, the grammatical operation is understood to apply to that suffix which follows it. Consequently, in the word *vārtraghnam*, there is no substitution of *t*. Now, if this is so...

In forms such as *mārṣṭibhyām*, the rule *anudātasya ca* would otherwise be unavoidable, because in the prescription of the suffix *am*, there is no apprehension of the verbal root (*dhātu*) by its own form. Regarding this, they say: based on a careful consideration of the Bhāṣya on the sūtra *mṛjer vṛddhiḥ*, it is established that "an operation stated with respect to a verbal root applies to a suffix attached to that [root]."

It should be explained that the insertion of the letter *t* is for the purpose of indicating that [the word] "bhavati" [is understood]; thus, there is no fault whatsoever. In the case of the word *arayū*, when the suffix *aṇ* follows, *yv-ādi* (the *y* and following sounds) is substituted as an irregularity (*nipātana*).
Water existing in the Sarayū is called *ārava*. The descendant of Ikṣvāku is *Ṭhaikṣvākaḥ*.

From the word *anapada*, the suffix *añ* is applied after a *kṣatriya* name; the elision (*lopa*) of *u* and *ū* occurs by virtue of a specific grammatical rule (*nipātana*). [The form] *aikṣvākuṣu* refers to what exists in the *janapada* (territory) of the Ikṣvākus. By the rule *opadhādaṇ*, [the suffix] *aṇ* is applied, resulting in *aikṣvākaḥ*. Here too, the elision of *u* occurs precisely by virtue of a specific rule (*nipātana*), because both forms ending in *añ* and *aṇ* are recited with a single phonetic unity (*ekaśruti*). However, in the case of the plural...

The distinction is that the suffix *ṭhañ* undergoes elision (*luk*) because it belongs to the *tadrāja* class, whereas *ṭhaṇ* does not. Thus says Raghunātha: "In the sense of 'descendant of Ikṣvāku' (*aikṣvākaḥ*). Murāri, however, says: "May our blessings bear fruit today among the descendants of Ikṣvāku and among the Maithilas. [The word] *hiraṇya* means a modification of gold.

*hiraṇmayaḥ* (golden). Here, the elision of the portion beginning with *y* is prescribed as a grammatical anomaly (*nipātana*) when the suffix *mayaṭ* is applied. (940) *yaskādibhyo gotre* (Pāṇini 2.4.63):

after [the words] *yaska* and others, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] in the sense of lineage (*gotra*). Since this falls outside the governing rule for "descendants" (*apatya*), the term *gotra* here is understood in its worldly, conventional sense.

With this intention, he says: "of the suffix denoting offspring" (*apatyapratyayasya*). From the rule *ṇyakṣatriyārṣe*, the word *luk* (elision) is understood to carry over; and from the rule *adrājasya*, as well as *ahuṣu tenaivāstriyām*. Therefore, he says: "there should be elision," and so forth. [The phrase] "caused by that" (*tatkṛte*)...

What [is the result]? *priyayāskaḥ*. What [is the result] when there is plurality? *yāskāḥ*. [The suffix] *dyañ* is applied after *śiva*, *yaska*, *luhya*, *druhya*, *karṇāṭaka*, *vasti*, *kudri*, *mitrayu*, and so forth.
(941) [Apatronymics are formed with the suffix *ṇya*] also after *atri*, *bhṛgu*, *kutsa*, *vasiṣṭha*, *gotama*, and *aṅgiras*. 2.4.65.

Regarding "of the patronymic suffix belonging to the Atri lineage": from the word *atri*, the suffix *ḍhak* is applied according to the rule *ṭhitaśca’niñaḥ*; however, it should be understood that for other [lineages], the suffix *ṛṣyaṇ* is applied. He provides an example from the Bhārata lineage:

(942) *bahvaca iñaḥ prācyabharateṣu* | Pāṇini 2.4.66. [This sūtra prescribes the elision of the suffix *iñ* when it follows a stem with many vowels (*bahvac*) belonging to the Easterners (*prācya*) or the Bhāratas.]

Regarding *yudhiṣṭhira*: the elision (*luk*) occurs only when there are many [descendants]. It does not occur here—*yaudhiṣṭhiriḥ*—because the suffix *iñ* is applied by virtue of its belonging to the *bāhv-ādi* group, thereby overriding the *ṇya* suffix which is characteristic of the *kuru* group. (943) *Na gopavanādibhyaḥ* | Pāṇini 2.4.67.
The meaning is that since this belongs to the *vidādi* subgroup, the elision (*luk*) prescribed by the rule *ṭhyañañośca* would apply here. (944) *tikakitavādibhyo dvandve* | 2|4|68|.
Although the words *tika*, *kitava*, and so forth are recited in the list as *dvandva* compounds themselves...

The *pūrvapadas* (first members) are "tik" and so forth, while the *uttarapadas* (second members) are "kitava" and so forth. Nevertheless, if it were stated as "from *ik* and so forth," one might suspect that the elision (*luk*) applies only to the *pūrvapadas*; however, it is intended to apply to the *uttarapadas* as well. Therefore, it is stated as "from *ik*, *kitava*, and so forth. Thus, [the compound] is *tikakitavāḥ*.

Others should also be cited here: the Āupakāyanas and the Lāmakāyanas; by the rule *aḍādibhyaḥ phak*, there is the elision (*luk*) of that suffix, resulting in *upakalamakāḥ*. The Bhrāṣṭrakayas and the Kāpiṣṭhalayas; by the rule *ata iñ*, there is the elision of that suffix, resulting in *bhrāṣṭrakakapiṣṭhalāḥ*. And the Kārṣṇājinayas.

And [the suffix] *cha* is applied after *kārṣṇasundara*. By the rule "after *ṭha*, *iñ* is applied," there is elision (*luk*) of that [suffix]. Examples include *kṛṣṇājina* and *kṛṣṇasundara*, and so forth.
(945) In a *dvandva* compound, [the suffix *cha*] is optionally applied after words beginning with *upaka*. Pāṇini 2.4.69.

The mention of "not a *dvandva*" (*advandva*) is for the purpose of making it clear that the term "*dvandve*" does not govern this rule. Among the *upaka* group, three *dvandva* compounds—such as *upakalamakāḥ* and others—are recited in the *atikakitavādi* class;
for these, there is obligatory elision (*luk*) by the preceding rule when they are not *dvandva*s.
Thus, it should be understood that there is an option (vikalpa) here.

Regarding the example "hrāṣṭrakikāpiṣṭhalayaḥ" in the Bhāṣya, Kaiyaṭa states that its inclusion among the *atikakitava* and other groups is not based on the ancient tradition (*anārṣa*). Therefore, even in this case of a *dvandva* compound, an option alone is appropriate.

With this intention, he provides an example: *bhrāṣṭrakakapiṣṭhalāḥ*, etc. With the intention that for those words listed in the *tikakitavādi* group, an option is appropriate only when they do not form a *dvandva* compound, he provides an example: *bhrāṣṭrakakapiṣṭhalāḥ*, etc., [from] the *tikakitavādi* group.
With the intention that for those [names] already recited, there is an option only when they are not *dvandva* compounds, he provides examples:
*lāmakāḥ*, *lāmakāyanāḥ*. In this same way, others should also be cited: *upakāḥ*, *aupakāyanāḥ*;
*bhrāṣṭrakāḥ*, *bhraṣṭrakāyanāḥ*, and so forth.
(946) *Āgastyakauṇḍinyayor agastikuṇḍinac* [Pāṇini 2.4.70]. From the word *āgastya*, there is the suffix *ṛṣyaṇ*; from the word *kuṇḍinī*, there is the suffix *yañ*. Now, one might object:
when the suffix *yañ* is applied to the word *kuṇḍinī*, by the rule *hasyāḍhea* [Pāṇini 6.3.42], the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*) would apply; however, by the rule *na taddhite* [Pāṇini 1.1.65]...

The elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant) would result. Nor should one suspect that the *prakṛtibhāva* (non-application of grammatical operations) applies here by the rule "and [a word] beginning with a conjunct consonant," because the term *ṭhaṇ* is understood to carry over in that rule. It is not so; for precisely because of this specific irregularity (*nipātana*), the form *kauṇḍinyaḥ* is established even without the application of that rule. Furthermore, the particle *ca* is for the sake of making the word end-acute (*antodātta*); for otherwise, it would be middle-acute (*madhyodātta*).

The word *kuṇḍinī*. Because the suffix *ni* in the sense of possession (*matvarthīya*) is udātta, the substitute *kuṇḍina* is also middle-udātta due to its closest phonetic proximity (*āntaratamya*). As for the remainder...

Regarding the phrase "of the base portion": one should not argue that only the substitution [of the base] for the entire complex including the suffix should be prescribed, rather than prescribing elision (*luk*). For if elision were applied, in the case of *agastīyāś chātrāḥ* ("the students of Agasti"), the suffix *cha* would be established by virtue of the [base] being designated as "vṛddha," since the elision is prohibited by the rule *otre'lugacī*.

However, if the rule for the substitute were applied to that which is qualified by the condition [of being a descendant], then upon the removal of the status of being a *vṛddha*, there would be the suffix *ñyaṇ* [by P.
4.1.101]. As for the form *kauṇḍināśchātrāḥ*, it is established in both ways;
for there is no difference in that case, as the suffix *aṇ*—which is the exception to the suffix *cha*—is applicable by the rule *aṇvādibhyo gotre* (P. 4.1.103).

(947) *rāja-śvaśurād yat* |4|1|137|. From *rājan* and *śvaśura*, the suffix *yat* [is applied]. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the [suffixes] *aṇ* and *iñ* respectively. It should be stated that [the suffix *yat* after *rājan*] applies only when denoting a genus (*jāti*). "Only when denoting a genus. [This is the] base form (*prakṛti*).

The meaning is that if the birth [of a person] is to be expressed by the collection of suffixes, then the suffix itself denotes only the offspring (*apatya*). Thus, the resulting sense is that [the term *gotra*] is both etymological and conventional (*yogarūḍha*), like the word *paṅkaja* ("lotus"). (948) *an* 6.4.167.

"Ṭilopa na" means that the elision of *ṭi* which was applicable by the rule "astaddhite" [Pāṇini 6.4.149] does not take place. (949) Regarding the rule "brāhmaṇāt saṃjñāyām" [Pāṇini 5.1.124], the word "brāhmaṇāt" is used in the sense of "in the case of a genus" (*jātau*). There is a separation of the yoga (*yogavibhāga*) here; for if it were a single yoga, [the result would be different].

By virtue of the capacity of the initial undertaking [of the rule], even though the elision of *ṭi* would be established for the word *brāhmī* when it refers to a non-jāti (non-genus), the form *brāhmaṇa* would not be established; for, due to the prohibition "when preceded by *a*, in the sense of offspring" (*a-mapūrvo ’patye*), the elision of *ṭi* would be unavoidable under the rule for *prakṛtibhāva* (*ṭhan*). Furthermore, in the case of a non-jāti...

The meaning is that [the form] *brāhmam* and so forth would not be established, because the *prakṛtibhāva* (non-application of suffixal changes) by the rule *ṭhan* would be unavoidable. Regarding *brāhma*: here, the term "in the sense of offspring" (*apatye*) is not connected; otherwise, this irregular derivation (*nipātana*) would be purposeless, as [the form would already be established] by the rule *a mapūrve*.

With the intention that the elision of *i* (*ṭilopa*) is established by the prohibition of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*), he says: "in the sense of non-descendant, when [the suffix] *aṇ* [is applied]. Regarding the word *brāhmam*: examples such as *brāhmaḥ muhūrtaḥ* and *brāhmaḥ sthālīpākaḥ* are also to be cited.
Now, even so, the form *brāhmaṇaḥ* would not be established, because of the rule "not preceded by *a*" (*nañpūrvaḥ*).

Because the natural state (*prakṛti-bhāva*) is prohibited, the elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel) would apply by the rule "a-taddhite" [Pāṇini 6.4.151] when the suffix *aṇ* is used in the sense of offspring (*apatya*). Therefore, he says: "in the sense of a genus (*jāti*). Here, by means of a "frog-leap" (*maṇḍūkapluti*), the words "in the sense of offspring" (*apatye*) and "not" (*na*) are carried over. This is what he expresses by saying "in the sense of offspring, in the sense of a genus," and so forth. The meaning here is as follows: "in the sense of offspring, in the sense of a genus..."

"In the word *brāhmaṇa*, the elision of the *ṭi* [suffix] does not occur. Some here, having split the rule as "ṭhāj jātau," explain it as "it does not occur when *ā* follows. However, in that interpretation, the term "e" should not be carried over [from the previous rule]. Why "in the sense of a genus"? [Consider: *brāhmāya nāradaḥ*.

(950) *ṣapūrvahandhṛtarājñāmaṇi* [Pāṇini 6.4.135]. Regarding *tākṣṇa*: it is derived from the *śivādi* group, or by the rule *asyedam* (‘this belongs to that’), the suffix *aṇ* is applied. Regarding *tākṣṇya*: the suffix *aṇya* is applied according to the characteristic of the agent (*kārin*). Regarding *kulīna*: the suffix *kha* is applied after the word *kula*. When the word *kula* stands alone, [the suffix *kha* is applied].

With the intention that the suffix *kha* is not superseded even by *yaṅ* and *kañ*, which are specifically prescribed by rules such as "after a word having *ṭha* as a prior member" (*ṭhapūrvapadāt*), because the phrase "optionally" (*anyatarasyām*) is included in their formulation, he says: (951) *kulātkhaḥ* | Pāṇini 4.1.139.

The phrase "it is because of the gender" (*liṅgāt*) means that otherwise, due to the prohibition of the rule regarding suffixes ending in *tad* (P. 1.1.72) in the case of *araṇavate*, the inclusion of the term "prior member" (*apūrvapada*) would be redundant; this is the intended meaning.
Regarding the example *āḍhyakulīnaḥ*: it is both *āḍhya* (wealthy) and *kulīna* (of noble birth), [the compound being formed] with *kulīna* as the qualifier.

The firmness of the family is not perceived; furthermore, the meaning is that there is also a distinction in accent, as the vowel *ī* is acute (*udātta*). (952) *Apūrvapadād anyatarasyāṃ yaṅ-ḍhak-au* | Pāṇini 4.1.140. [This rule provides for the optional application of the suffixes] *yaṅ* and *ḍhak* after a word that does not have another word as its prior member.

Regarding the term *bahukulya*: since the suffix *bahuc*—by the rule *vibhāṣā supaḥ*—is not a *pada*, and because it does not have a preceding word (*apūrvapadatvāt*), three suffixes apply; this is the intended meaning. (953) *vyant sapatne* 4.1.145.

"It would be lost" (*vyansyāt*): the meaning is that if the offspring of the brother were denoted by the suffix *śatru*, then [the word] would end in *bhrātṛ-śatru* and not in *bhrātṛ-vyaccha*. "By the whole" (*samudāyena*): the meaning is that when the derivative suffix in the form of *śatru*—which contains that [base *bhrātṛ*]—is to denote the offspring. As for what was stated by the author of the Vṛtti—"there is no sense of 'offspring' here at all"—[that is incorrect].
Setting aside that [objection] on the grounds that it contradicts the *Bhāṣya*, he says: "by the evil" (*pāpmanā*).

He explains the derivation of the word *bhrātṛvya* as used in the Śruti by saying: "figuratively" (*upacārāt*). Amara states: "The neuter *pāpman* and *pāpa* mean sin, guilt, or blemish. For indeed, sin...
The intention is that since [the word *bhrātṛ*] means "the offspring of a brother," this usage is merely figurative (*bhākta*).

(954) *Revatyādibhyaṣṭhak* | Pāṇini 4.1.146. [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after *revatī* etc. Examples: *Raivatika*, *Āśvapālaka*, *Māṇipālaka*, *Dvārapālaka*, and so forth. [By the rule] *ṭhasyekaḥ*, the *ṭha* is replaced by *ika*.

Because the term "of the *aṅga*" (*aṅgasya*) is understood [from the previous rule], it is stated: "following the *aṅga*. Since the letter *ṭh* is a qualifier of the suffix *ṭhak*, it does not apply to the *ṭh* of *aṭhac*. For example: *karmaṭhaḥ*.

(955) Pāṇini 4.1.147: *gotrastriyāḥ kutsane ṇa ca* ("After a feminine word denoting lineage (*gotra*), the suffix *ṇa* is applied, as well as [the suffixes previously mentioned], when contempt is expressed").

Regarding the feminine form *gotrastriyāḥ*: it should be understood that the suffix *ṅīp* is applied to *glucukāyanī*—as in the example "the wretched *glaucukāyana*, the offspring of *glucukāyanī*"—in order to ensure the *vṛddhi* strengthening of the vowel before the suffix *phin*. The phrase "by virtue of the sense" (*sāmārthyāt*) refers to the rule stating that "no further *gotra*-suffix follows another *gotra*-suffix."
The meaning is: "the offspring of Gārgī. There is contempt because she is designated by her mother's name when the father is unknown.

Why say "in the sense of a lineage" (gotre)? [Consider: *kārikeyo jālmaḥ* ("this wretch is the son of Kārikā"). Why say "of a female" (*striyāḥ*)? [Consider: *aupagavir jālmaḥ* ("this wretch is the offspring of Aupagava"). Why say "in the sense of contempt" (*kutsane*)? [Consider: *gārgeyaḥ*.
The young student says: (956) Pāṇini 4.1.150: *phāṇṭāhṛtimimatābhyāṃ ṇa-phiñau*.

[The suffix] *ṇa* is applied after *phāṇṭāhṛti*, and *phiñ* after *mimata*. The word *utsa* is no longer operative here. There is a specific purpose for the *ṇit*-designation (*ṇitva*) in the case of *vṛtimat*.

He provides an illustration while making this point: "In the opinion of my teacher" (*mama mata*). Nor should it be argued that even in the Bhāṣya’s view, the purpose of the marker *ṇ* in the word *haṇṭāhṛtābhāryaḥ*—namely, the prevention of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*) by the rule *vṛddhinimittasya*—is realized; for [the rule] *astriyām* [prevents this].

The meaning is as follows: because the designation *yuvan* is prohibited and the designation *gotra* exists, by the restrictive rule "there is only one [suffix] in the *gotra*," there is no further descendant after the word *phāṇṭāhṛti* which ends in the suffix *iñ*; consequently, the form *phāṇṭāhṛta* itself does not exist [as a base for further derivation].
(957) Pāṇini 4.1.151: *kurvādibhyo ṇyaḥ*.
The [suffix] *aṇ* after words such as *kuru* is also excluded by the rule "among the Āvīras. Thus, one says *kauravyā brāhmaṇāḥ*.

However, regarding what will be stated later—that the suffix *ṇya* occurs after *uru* and others—since that is a *tadrāja* (patronymic) suffix, it undergoes elision (*luk*) when applied to many [descendants], resulting in *uravaḥ kṣatriyāḥ*, and not *auravyāḥ*; this is the intended meaning.

Regarding *vāvadūkyā*: the suffix *ūka* is added to the reduplicated form of *vada*. They say that this occurs here in this very list due to a formal exception (*nipātana*). [The bases are: *kuru*, *garga*, and *vāvadūka*. Regarding *samrājaḥ kṣatriye*:

the meaning is that the suffix *ṇya* is added to the word *samrāj* when referring to a Kṣatriya. "In the case of *vāmaratha*, [the formation] is like that of the *kaṇva* group, with the exception of the accent."

Whatever grammatical operation applies to the word *kāvyá*, which ends in the suffix *yañ*, would also apply to the word *vāmarathyá*, which ends in the suffix *ṇya*. This means [the operation applies] except for the case where it is acutely accented on the first syllable (*ādyaudāta*). In the plural, there is elision (*luk*) by the rule "of *yañ* and *añ* after a Bahuvrīhi. Thus: *vāmarathāḥ chātrāḥ* (the students of Vāmaratha). Here, the suffix *aṇ*—which is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *cha* prescribed by the rule "after *aṇ* etc., in the sense of a *gotra*"—is applied. Thus: *vāmarathī*.

The feminine form is *vāmarathyāyanī*. [This is derived] by the application of the suffixes *ṅīṣ* and *ṣpha*, according to the rules *ṭhyañaśca* and *rācāṃ ṣpha taddhitaḥ*. The collective group (*saṅgha*), numerical category (*aṅka*), and characteristic mark (*lakṣaṇa*) are called *vāmarathāni*. Here, the suffix *aṇ*—which is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *cha*—is applied according to the rule *aṅghāṅkalakṣaṇeṣu*. Examples include *satyaṅkāra*, *valabhīkāra*, *buddhikāra*, and so forth.

(958) *senāntalakṣaṇakāribhyaśca* || 4.1.152 || *Hāriṣeṇyaḥ*: Since the rule *ṭhak cati saṃjñāyām* [Pāṇini 4.1.153] renders the substitution of *ṣ* as not yet established (*asiddha*), this word ends in *senā*.

*Tākṣṇaḥ*: An addition (*upasaṅkhyāna*) is made for the suffix *aṇ* after *tākṣan*. *Tākṣṇaḥ*: This *aṇ* is an exception (*bādhaka*) to the *iñ* suffix prescribed by the Northern Grammarians (*udīcām*).
From this supplementary enumeration (*upasaṅkhyāna*), it is understood that the reading of the word *takṣan* among the *śiva*-group [of words] is not based on the original scripture (*anārṣa*).

However, the author of the Vṛtti, having read the word *takṣan* among the *śiva*-group, states: "This [suffix] characterized by *ari* (i.e., *aṇ*) subverts the *iñ* suffix prescribed for the Udīcya region; but as for the *ṇa* suffix, its subversion..."
"It is not so intended," he says; in accordance with that, we too have explained it in that very way there, because there is no difference in the result.
[Pāṇini 4.1.155] *Kauśalya-kārma-āryebhyaś-ca*.

The meaning is this: [the formation] *kauśalya* arises precisely from the word *paramaprakṛti* (the ultimate base). However, if this rule were to apply from the word *kośala* ending in *ñyaṅ* according to the rule "vṛddhetkosalādibhyaśca," or from the word *karmāra* ending in the suffix *ṇya* which characterizes the agent, then it would result in the application [of the suffix] only in the sense of a descendant (*yuvan*). This is the intended point.
[This applies] also to *chāga* and *vṛṣa*. Regarding the word *chāga*: this is also an elliptical expression (*upalakṣaṇa*) for the word *dagu*.

This is because of the Vārttika in the section on the suffix *phañ*: “In the case of *agu*, *kosala*, *karmāra*, *chāga*, and *vṛṣa*, there is the addition of *yuṭ* [before the suffix], and [the substitution of] *ādiṣṭa*. Regarding “of *ādiṣṭa*”: the meaning is “of that which has the substitute ending in *āyan*.”

Otherwise, if the suffix *yu* were applied as prescribed by the rule for the nominal stem itself, then because it would not begin with a suffix, the substitution of *āyana* for *pha* would not occur in forms such as *kauśalyāyaniḥ*;
however, when *yuk* is applied, as in *āgavyāyaniḥ*, the substitution of *guṇa* for *au* does take place.
The intention is that elsewhere there would be neither [the substitution of] *ay* nor the elision (*allopa*) of the vowel.
(960) Aṇo dvyacaḥ | Pāṇini 4.1.156. Regarding "Kārtrāyaṇi": the offspring of Karta is Kārtra; the offspring of that [Kārtra] is Kārtrāyaṇi. In this case...

They explain: the word *kartṛ* is read as *kurv-ādi* (belonging to the *kurv-ādi* group) with a genitive ending (*ṣaṣṭhī*). Thus, Vardhamāna has cited only ‘*ārtryaḥ*’; therefore, in this context, examples such as *bhartṛhartryaḥ* should be cited. As for *dākṣiḥ*, [it is formed] by [the rule] ‘*vā nāmadheyasya*’.

This is a counter-example under the view that the designation *vṛddha* does not apply; however, under the other view, the suffix *phiñ* certainly occurs. Amarasimha states: "The stars [beginning with] Ākṣāyaṇī and Aśvinī, etc. (4.1.157).
(961) "After *vākin* and others, there is also the suffix *kuk*. 4.1.158.

Regarding the *vākinādi* group: if a word-form here is "vṛddha" (belonging to the first three classes of vowels) and not a *gotra* (patronymic), this statement serves solely for the purpose of adding the augment (*āgama*);

however, for others, it serves both purposes. Because the term "udīcām" (of the Northern grammarians) is understood to follow, an option results; thus he says, "the suffix *phiñ* may optionally [be applied]. In the example *vākinakāyaniḥ*: *vākaḥ* means speech.

"One who has this" is *vākinaḥ*; for this very reason, the suffix *ini* is applied by irregular derivation (*nipātana*). "One who prospers in a house" (*agāre edhate*) is *gāredhaḥ*; the elision of the initial [syllable] occurs because it belongs to the *pṛṣodarādi* group, and the substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) occurs because it belongs to the *śakandhvādi* group.
From *gāredha* comes *gāredhakāyaniḥ*. In the case of *carmivarmi-ādi*, it is for the sake of both meanings; [the suffixes are added] from the words *carman* and *varman*.
The suffix *ini* is applied because [the word *carman*] belongs to the *vrīhy-ādi* group. There is a *gaṇa*-sūtra stating: “In the case of *carman* and *varman*, there is elision of the *n*.
Thus we have *cārmikāyaṇiḥ* and *vārmikāyaṇiḥ*.
When the suffix *ku* is added, since the *n* is no longer final, the elision of *n* would not otherwise apply; hence this rule is stated. Nor does *ku* [cause the elision].

It might be argued that [the suffix] *para* etc. should be applied; however, because *pha* is beginningless (*anādi*), there would be the undesirable consequence (*prasaṅga*) of the absence of the substitution of *āya*. [The form] *vākiniḥ* is derived by the rule *ata iñ*. In the absence of *phiñ*, the suffix *kuk*, which is prescribed as being conditioned by that (*tatsaṃniyogaśiṣṭa*), does not occur here. In the same way, *gāredhiḥ*, *cārmiṇaḥ*, and so forth, should be inferred.

(962) *putrāntād anyatarasyām* |4|1|159|. Since the intention is that [the word] *udīcāṃ vṛddhāt* is understood as continuing [from the previous rule], he says: "The suffix *phiñ* is established by that very rule; therefore, by this [present rule], only *kuñ* is optionally [applied]."
The sense is that it is prescribed.

(963) *prācām avṛddhāt phin bahulam* 4.1.160. [The rule begins: *prācām avṛddhāt*. The mention of "of the Easterners" (*prācām*) is for the sake of honor. Why [is it said] "from a non-vṛddha [stem]" (*avṛddhāt*)? What is the purpose?
*Rājadantī* (the woman whose teeth are like those of a king). *Bahvagrajaṇānneha*—*Dākṣiḥ* (the descendant of Dakṣa). (964) *Manoḥ jātāv añyatau ṣuk ca* |4|1|161|.
*Mānuṣaḥ* (human), *manuṣyaḥ* (human)—these two are words denoting a genus (*jāti*). [The suffix] *mūḍhe* [is applied] to denote a contemptible offspring.

The substitution of *manas* for *māna* is traditionally taught; furthermore, the change of the letter *n* to a retroflex (*mūrdhanya*) [nasal] is established by that [substitution], resulting in the form *māṇava*.

This is intended to prescribe the substitution of *ṇ*, since [the substitution of *ma* for *māna*] is already established by the rule *amaḥ*. His state of being a fool (*mūḍhatva*) results from not having studied the Vedas, and his state of being contemptible (*kutsitatva*) results from the non-performance of prescribed duties. And this statement [is made] regarding the term *brāhmaṇamāṇave*.
They say that [the form] is not obtained through the irregular substitution (*nipātana*).
(965) *janapada-śabdāt kṣatriyād añ* (Pāṇini 5.1.168). Regarding *janapada-kṣatriya*: the meaning is "that which denotes a country (*janapada*) and also denotes a Kṣatriya."

Although words such as *pāñcāla* and others take the plural ending when denoting a country (*janapada*), they take the singular ending when denoting a Kṣatriya; nevertheless, it should be understood that the capacity of the nominal stem (*prātipadika*) to denote both meanings remains intact. What is the purpose of [specifying] "from a word denoting a country"? [Consider: the descendant of Druhyu is *Drauhyavaḥ*.

This [suffix] denotes exclusively a Kṣatriya. Why say "from a Kṣatriya"? [Because otherwise it would apply to others; for example,] the Vṛttikāra and others hold that the offspring of a Brāhmaṇa Pañcāla is a Pāñcāli. Others, however, maintain that this counter-example is to be reconsidered, because this word is read among the *bāhv-ādi* group [and thus takes the suffix *iñ*].

[The suffix] is applied to a *janapada* (territory) whose name is identical to that of a *kṣatriya*, just as it is applied to the offspring of a *rājanya*. Regarding the phrase "whose name is identical to that of a *kṣatriya*":

a *janapada* whose name (*śabda*) is the same [as another] is a "janapada with an identical name. A *janapada* whose name is identical to a *kṣatriya* is a "janapada with a name identical to a *kṣatriya*."

Therefore, the meaning is that when "rājan" (king) is to be expressed, a suffix occurs after a word ending in the sixth case in the sense of "his," just as it does in the sense of "offspring. In the example "the king of the Pañcālas," the suffix *vuñ*, which would otherwise apply by the rule "even after a non-vṛddha [stem], when the referent is plural," is superseded.

Regarding *pūroḥ*: it must be stated that [the suffix] is applied after *pūru*. Since the word *pūru* does not denote a country (*janapada*), the suffix *aṇ* is already established by the rule for derivatives in the sense of "belonging to" (*prāgdīvyatīya*); therefore, this specific statement is made for the purpose of assigning it the technical name *tadrāja*.
If, however, it were to denote a country, it would have been established simply by the rule "*ṭhyañ magadha*" (Pāṇini 4.1.170).

The addition of the marker *ṇit* in the word *pāṇḍoḍaḷÇṇ* is for the purpose of prohibiting the masculine substitution (*puṃvadbhāva*) in a form such as *pāṇḍaḷabhāryaḥ*, by means of the rule "when [the suffix] is caused by a *vṛddhi* vowel. Here, the word *pāṇḍu* is not intended to refer to the father of Yudhiṣṭhira, nor does it denote a quality (*guṇa*).
When it is stated "from words that do not have *pada* as their final member," only those [words] expressing the overlord (*adhipati*) of that [region] are brought to mind.
Pāṇini 4.1.169: *sālveyagāndhāribhyāṃ ca* ("and from Sālveya and Gāndhāri").
[The rule applies when] there is *vṛddhi*. Why is the *tapara* marker used? [To exclude cases like] *kaumāraḥ*. For the word *kumārī*...
[This refers to] the designation of a *kṣatriya* belonging to a [specific] country (*janapada*). (967) *Kurunādibhyo ṇyaḥ* | Pāṇini 4.1.172.

[The group beginning with] Kuru and those whose initial sound is *n* are the "n-ādika" group. From the word *kuru*, when the suffix *aṇ* would otherwise apply by virtue of its having two syllables, [the suffix *ṇya* is applied instead].
When [the suffix] *añ* is applicable, this statement [is made] because [the suffix] *cha* would otherwise apply after words beginning with *nada*.
(968) *Sālvāvayava-pratyagratha-kalakūṭāśmakād-iñ*: 4.1.173. "The *udumbara*-class," etc.: "The *udumbaras*, the *tilakhalas*, the *madrakāras*, and the *yugaṃdharas*."
The commentary states: "Bhrūliṅga, Śaradaṇḍa, and those designated as parts of Sālva.
Examples to be cited include Āuḍumbari, Tailakhali, Mādrakāri, Yaugandhari, and so forth.

(969) *te tadrājāḥ* |4|1|174|. "Those beginning with *añ* are called *tadrāja*. Those that precede them are not referred to by the word "those" (*tacchabdena*), because of the interruption caused by the section on the technical designations of *gotra* and *yuvan*. It is precisely for this purpose [that the rule is stated].
Some say that this section was placed in the middle by the Teacher. In reality, however,

others maintain that there is no harm even if the section on the technical designations *gotra* and *yuvan* is not recited in the middle, because it begins with the rules starting from "under the heading of *adrāja*, [the suffix] *añ* is applied after a *kṣatriya* name that does not end in a word denoting a [specific] status (*anapada-śabda*)," and so forth.

(970) *tadrājasya bahuṣu tenaivā’striyām* || 2.4.62 || Regarding the rule *tadrājasya*: the phrase *tadarthena* means "formed by the meaning of that *tadrāja* suffix. Why [is it said] *tenaiva* ("by that very same [suffix]")? [Consider the example: *priyapāñcālāḥ*. As for the phrase *sādhava iti*: likewise, [it refers to the sense expressed by] "one who is skilled (*sādhuh*) in this."
The sense is that because the suffix [denoting] a descendant lacks the status of being a *tadrāja* (a patronymic denoting a king), there is no elision (*luk*).

Since the words *raghu* and *yadu* do not denote a country (*janapada*), the designation *tadrāja* does not apply to the suffixes following them; thus, due to the non-application of elision, the forms remain as *rāghavāṇām* and *yādavaiḥ*.
Anticipating the objection that [the suffix] must exist, he says: "of the words *raghu* and *yadu*. He says: "by means of figurative indication (*lakṣaṇayā*).
The meaning is that, because the sense has already been expressed, the patronymic suffix (*apatyapratyaya*) is not produced here. (971) *kambojālluk* | Pāṇini 4.1.175.

Regarding *kambojāl luk*: this [rule] has not been placed within the very section beginning with "when there are many" (*bahuṣu*), because otherwise there would be the undesirable consequence (*prasaṅga*) that the suffix *añ* expressing two or one objects would not undergo elision (*luk*).

Even though, by virtue of the force of prescribing elision again under the heading of elision (*luka-adhikāra*), elision will indeed occur for the *añ* even when it expresses two or one, [the rule is stated here for that specific purpose].

It can indeed be said; nevertheless, they maintain that it was not included in the section on *cha* because there is a risk of the elision (*luk*) applying even to non-descendants (*atadrāja*), and furthermore, there is no economy of effort [in doing so]. Nor is it the case here that the word "Ambhoja" refers to a descendant only by way of secondary indication (*lakṣaṇā*).
One might object: "Since forms such as *kamboja* are established [by other rules], what is the purpose of this sūtra?
This objection is to be set aside, because the sūtra is necessary to prevent undesirable optional forms such as *amboja*.
It should be stated: "from *kamboja* and others. Regarding *sindhu-takṣa*: [this refers to] the word *kamboja*.

The suffix *aṇ* is applied because [the word] belongs to the *sindhv-ādi* group; however, the intention is that since it does not denote a descendant (*tadrāja*), the feminine suffix *ṅīp* does not apply. (Pāṇini 4.1.176) *striyām avantikuntikurubhyaśca*: [The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after the words] *avanti*, *kunti*, and *kuru*. When the suffix *ñyaṅ* is elided by the rule "after a word ending in a long vowel" (*vṛddhe*), [the feminine suffix is applied] because of the presence of the *it* marker.

In the case of *manuṣyajāti*, the suffix *ṅī* is applied; in *kurūḥ*, the suffix *ṇya* is elided, and by the rule *ṭhūRutaḥ*, the suffix *ūṅ* is applied. (973) *ataśca* |4|1|177|. Here, the vowel *a* is qualified by the term *tadrāja*, but the term *tadrāja* is not qualified by the vowel *a*.

If the rule of *tadanta-vidhi* (extension of a grammatical operation to that which ends with the specified element) were applied by means of the qualifier (*viśeṣaṇa*), then since suffixes such as *ñyaṅ* and *ṇya* would also end in *a* and be *tadrāja*, their elision (*luk*) would be established by this very [rule]; consequently, the sūtra "striyām avantī" (Pāṇini 4.1.173), which prescribes the elision for *Avanti*, *Kunti*, and *Kuru*, would become redundant. And this is not desired.
[The author] explains [the rule], because otherwise forms such as *apatih* and *kausalya* would result in incorrect derivations.

(974) Pāṇini 4.1.178: "Not after [tribes] beginning with Bharga or Yaudheya, when the suffix is *tadrāja* ending in *a*. The intention is that the inclusion of the long vowel marker (*tapara*) in the sūtra is for the sake of clarity.

Regarding *śūrasenī*: when the suffix *aṇ* is elided, the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied by the rule "ātaḥ" (Pāṇini 4.1.40), provided that the word does not end in *añ*. It is not the suffix *ṅīn* prescribed for words ending in *añ*, because the commentary explains [the rule] as "for a word ending in the *a*-sound of the suffix *ṭhañ*. Regarding *kārūśī*: from the root *kṛ*, the form *karuḥ* is derived with the suffix *u*;
one who desires (*vaṣṭi*) that is a *karuśaḥ*. The suffix *ka* is applied by the rule "mūlavibhujādi" (Vārttika on Pāṇini 3.2.5) to the root *vaś* meaning "to desire."

In the word *rāhijya*, there is a vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Its descendant is *rājā* or *kāruśaḥ*; in the feminine, it is *kārūśī*. By this, a reading with a retroflex sibilant (*mūrdhanya*) as the penultimate letter is rejected. To provide an illustration of the prohibition of elision (*luk*) for the *yaudheya* group, he says: "from *yudhāṃśas*, *śukra*, etc. [This occurs] when there is elision by the rule *ataśca*.

The sense is that since it will be stated later that "those ending in *ñi* and so forth are *tadrāja*," this *añ* suffix possesses the status of a *tadrāja*. With the intention that the suffix *ṅīṣ* does not apply because the word ends in a consonant (*yopadha*), he says: "in the case of *ṅīp*.

Regarding the term "the accent for the removal of the acute" (*udātanivṛttisvara*), it refers to the rule: "And [the acute accent is applied] to an unaccented vowel where there is the elision of an acute vowel."

The meaning is that the feminine suffix *ṅīp* would be udātta (accented). However, it should be understood that according to the established conclusion (*siddhānta*), because there is no elision (*luk*) of the suffix *aṇ*, the udāttatva belongs to the initial syllable of the *ṅīn* suffix. This might be argued: let the elision (*luk*) prescribed by the rule "ataśca" apply only to those *tadrāja* suffixes that have four meanings (*cāturarthika*).
Because of proximity, [the term *tadrāja*] refers to those [suffixes] taught in the fifth book (Pāṇini 4.1.173ff) by the rule "but *ṭhak*, *ñya*, etc., are *tadrāja*";
so what is the purpose of this mention of *yaudheya* and others? True;
it is to indicate that, according to the principle of pervasion (*vyāptinyāya*), the suffixes taught in the fifth book are also to be understood here.

The mention of *yaudheya* and others is for this purpose: by it, the elision (*luk*) of the feminine suffix after the *aṇ* [secondary suffix] derived from *pārśva* and similar names is established. For instance, *parśu* is a name for a Kṣatriya that is identical in form to a country name. Its female descendant is formed with the suffix *aṇ* by the rule *vyañ-mahad-ādibhyaś ca*; then, by the rule *ṭhaś-ca*, there is elision of that [suffix]. Subsequently, the characteristic [suffixes] of *parśvādi* apply.

The suffix *aṇ* is used here in its own sense (*svārthika*). When that [suffix] also undergoes elision (*luk*), by the rule "after a word ending in *ū* or *ṛ*, [the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied]," we have *parśūḥ*. Similarly, the female descendant of a *rakṣas* who is a Kṣatriya is *rakṣāḥ*. As before, when both *aṇ* suffixes are elided, there is lengthening by the rule "of a word ending in *at* or *as*. And it has been stated by the author of the Vārttika: "From *parśu* and others..."

The elision (*luk*) [of the feminine suffix] should be stated; or rather, the prohibition regarding *yaudheya* and others is an indicator (*jñāpaka*) that there is elision after *pārśva* and so on—as in *yaudheyī* and similar forms. The analysis of the compound is: "the female descendant (*apatyam strī*) of *yudhāyāḥ* or *śukrāyāḥ*.

(975) Pāṇini 4.1.78: *aṇiñoranārṣayorgururūpotamayoḥ ṣyaṅ gotre*. [The feminine suffix] *ṣyaṅ* is applied in the sense of a lineage (*gotra*) after [stems ending in] the suffixes *aṇ* or *iñ*, provided they are not Vedic names (*anārṣa*), have a heavy syllable (*guru*) as their penultimate (*upotama*), and end in *u*.
Regarding *aṇiñoḥ*: [the word] *uttama* is an unanalyzed (*avyutpanna*) nominal stem (*prātipadika*), and it is not derived from the word *ud* with the suffix *tamap*.
Therefore, one should not suspect that the suffix *ām* applies by the rule *imetiṅvyayaghādām*. Regarding *gotre yau*:

since the governing topic is "progeny" (*apatya*), and because of the principle that "elsewhere than in the context of progeny, 'lineage' (*gotra*) refers to the worldly [usage]," the technical (*śāstrīya*) definition of lineage is not intended here.

And thus, since the desired result is already established by the very exclusion (*paryudāsa*) in the rule *ṭhañ ārṣeḥ*, the mention of *gotra* here could have been omitted. Nor should it be argued that, by the force of the mention of *gotra* in this context, only a technical (grammatical) *gotra* is intended; for forms such as *daivadatyā* and *yājñadatyā* are desired even when the suffix applies to an immediate descendant (*ānantarāpatya*).
For this very reason, he will state immediately following [this rule]: "The female descendant of Umudagandhi is *kaumudagandhyā*.
This explanation, which follows the *Kaustubha*, is consistent with the root text (*mūla*) at this point;
however, it contradicts the root text found in the sūtra on *aiṣukāri* and others, which states: "The suffix *ṭhak* is for the purpose of denoting a lineage (*gotra*)," and so forth.

This will become clear in that very context. Although feminine suffixes (*strīpratyaya*) are the subject under discussion, nevertheless, just as in the case of the *nakāra* in the rule "atyurno yajñasaṃyoge," it is more appropriate for *ṣyaṅ* to be an *ādeśa* (substitute) rather than a suffix; this is because the genitive case in the rule "ṭhaṇiñoḥ" suggests such an interpretation. With this intention, he says: "it should be an *ādeśa* of *ṣyaṅ*."
It is established in the *Manoramā* that even though *ṣyaṅ* is a suffix (*pratyaya*), the derivation of the form is unimpeded.

Now, one might object: this [suffix] would be a replacement for the whole (*sarvādeśa*) rather than a partial replacement (*avatsarvādeśa*), because it would supersede the substitution of *icc* (the *it* marker), since the rule "icc" finds its application in cases such as *in-aṅ* and others which serve no other purpose.

Anticipating the objection that the two markers (anubandhas) serve a purpose as qualifiers for the rule "ṭhyaṅścābit" (Pāṇini 6.1.71), which applies to both *ṣyaṅ* and *ṭhyaṅ*, he says: "of that which is being specifically indicated" (*nirdiśyamānasya*). He adds: "the two markers are [present] in *ṣyaṅ* just as they are in *ñyaṅ*. This indicates that the employment of the two markers is intended to apply to *ṣyaṅ* in the same manner as to *ñyaṅ*.

In the rule *ṭhyaṅśca āp*, the mention of *ṭhyaṅ* is for the purpose of including the general category; it has no utility as a qualifier in the rule *yaṅaḥ saṃprasāraṇam*. Otherwise, even in the case of *pāśyāputraḥ* and *pāśyāpatiḥ*, where the suffix *ya* is applied by the rule *āśādibhyo yaḥ*, [the same problem would arise].

It should be stated that there is the contingency of *saṃprasāraṇa* [occurring here as well], because even by means of the rule "ṭhyaṅḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pāṇini 6.1.13), which contains a single indicatory letter (*anubandha*), that [contingency] is prevented. However, in the case of "aulūyāpati," there is an absence of *saṃprasāraṇa* due to the intervention of the suffix *akāra*. [As for] "aumudagandhīputra"—
In this case, however, because the single-substitute (ekādeśa) is treated as belonging to the end of the preceding element, there is no intervention;
thus, the *saṃprasāraṇa* is established. [The examples are: *kaumudagandhyā*—here *ṣyaṅ* is applied after *aṇ*;

*vārāhyā*—here *ṣyaṅ* is applied after *iñ*. Why "after *aṇ* and *iñ*"? [Counter-example: *ārtabhāgī*, the descendant of *Ṛtubhāga*; here *añ* is applied because [the name] belongs to the *bidādi* group.

The suffix *ṅīn* is applied by the rule "ār̥ṅgaravādyañaḥ"; however, the author of the Vṛtti maintains that the suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule "iḍḍhea" etc. In the rule "ṭhaṇiñoḥ," the term "gotra" refers to the worldly (secular) lineage; but in the rule "gotraṃ ca caraṇaiḥ," only the technical (grammatical) definition is intended. Therefore—

They state the solution for the established position that, because it lacks the status of a *jāti*, there is no application of the suffix *ṅīp*: [Pāṇini 4.1.79] "After a word denoting a lineage (*gotra*) which is a subordinate part.
Regarding "after a word denoting a lineage which is a subordinate part": the word "subordinate part" (*avayava*) signifies what is not primary; thus, it is both a subordinate part and a lineage.

This is a *karmadhāraya* compound; due to irregular derivation (*nipātana*), the word *gotra* is placed first. "Those considered *gotras*" means those who are regarded as such—that is, those well-known in specific regions by virtue of being called *gotras*, but not those recited in the *Pravarādhyāya*.
Furthermore, their lack of preeminence is due to their not being recited in the *Pravarādhyāya*. Regarding the term "family-designations" (*kulākhyā*):
they are called "family-designations" because by them the family is designated—such as Puṇika, Bhuṇika, Mukhara, and so forth.
For it is by means of these that the family is designated, as in: "We are Puṇikas by lineage," or "We are Huṇikas by lineage."
Then [the word] *iti* [is used]. The meaning is "from a portion of a lineage" (*gotrāvayavāt*).
(977) *Krauḍy-ādibhyaś-ca* | 4.1.80. Regarding *krauḍy-ādibhyaś-ca*, since the fifth case ending (*pañcamī*) is specified, it is understood here that these are indeed suffixes; thus he says—*ṣyaṅ*.

Regarding the term *pratyaya*: [the examples are] Krauḍi, Vyāḍi, Āpiśali, Gaukakṣya, and so forth. The word *gaukakṣya* ends in the suffix *yañ* from the *garga*-class; he states its purpose [with the rule]: "and for the sake of that which does not end in *aṇ* or *iñ*. Regarding *sūta*: this is a *gaṇa*-sūtra. The word *sūta* receives the suffix *ṣyaṅ* when denoting a young woman.

The meaning is "in the case of that which is to be expressed [by the feminine suffix]. Regarding *sūtyā*: both *ṣyaṅ* and *ṭhyaṅ* [apply]. But elsewhere, the suffix *ṭāp* applies after a word denoting an action (*kriyāśabda*). However, for a word denoting the *sūta* caste, the suffix *ṅīṣ* applies, as in *sūtī*. Regarding *bhojī*: this is also a *gaṇasūtra*. It is an exception (*apavāda*) to the *ṅīṣ* prescribed by the rule for generic names (*jātilakṣaṇa*), and it applies after a word denoting an action.
*Ṭāp* itself— [as in] *bhojyā*, meaning "she who causes to eat.
(978) *Daivayajñi-śaucivṛkṣi-sātyamugri-kāṇḍeviddhi-bhyo ’nyatarasyām* | Pāṇini 4.1.81.

Regarding *dauvayajñi*: the phrase "from four" (*caturbhyaḥ*) implies "from those ending in *ṭhiñ*. One for whom the gods are the sacrifices to be performed is *devayajñaḥ*. One whose tree is pure is *śucivṛkṣaḥ*. One whose fierce [quality] is truth is *satyamugraḥ*; due to irregular derivation (*nipātana*), the qualifier is placed first and the augment *mum* is added. By means of a section (*kāṇḍena*).
*Kaṇṭheviddhaḥ* means "pierced in the throat. The compound is formed according to the rule *kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā* (Pāṇini 2.1.32).

Due to irregularity (*nipātana*), the word *kāṇḍa* takes the form *kaṇṭha*. In an alternative reading, *kaṇṭheviddhaḥ* means either "one whose [arrow] is fixed in the throat" or "one who is pierced in the throat. The elision of the case-ending does not occur here, as indicated by the rule *mūrdhamastakādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.3.14). From all these [words], the suffix is applied in the sense of a descendant (*apatya*).
"Because it is subsequent, [the suffix] applies even to *gotra*. Thus, the intention is that there is an option (*vibhāṣā*) in both cases.

Here, this should be noted: if "lineage" (*gotra*) is understood in the sense of the technical grammatical lineage (*śāstrīya-gotra*) in the rule *aṇiñoḥ*, then the passage beginning with "this is for the sake of non-lineage" (*agotrārtham idam*) and so forth accords naturally with its own intent. However, if...

In that context, only the worldly lineage (*laukika-gotra*) is understood; therefore, since [the suffix] would necessarily apply by the rule *ṭhaṇiñoḥ*, it is not appropriate to explain this [sūtra] as being for the sake of an option (*vikalpa*). Thus ends the section on offspring (*apatya-adhikāra*) in the *Tattvabodhinī*.

(1279) *prāgvateṣṭhañ* | Pāṇini 5.1.18.
